questions.prompt: A parking garage charges $3 for each hour or part of an hour, so C(t) = 3⌈t⌉ dollars for 0 < t ≤ 4 hours, where ⌈t⌉ is the least integer greater than or equal to t. Which graph shows C?
questions.prompt_markup: A parking garage charges $3 for each hour or part of an hour, so C(t) = 3⌈t⌉ dollars for 0 < t ≤ 4 hours, where ⌈t⌉ is the least integer greater than or equal to t. Which graph shows C?
questions.grading_note: Any part of an hour costs a full $3: 0 < t ≤ 1 costs 3, so the first step is open at t = 0 and closed at t = 1 (exactly 1 hour costs $3, not $6). The others close the wrong ends, use rounding down (3⌊t⌋), or charge for exact fractions of an hour (3t).

questions.prompt: A parking garage charges $3 for each hour or part of an hour, up to a maximum of $15 per day. ⌈t⌉ is the least integer greater than or equal to t. Which rule gives the cost C(t) for 0 < t ≤ 24 hours?
questions.prompt_markup: A parking garage charges $3 for each hour or part of an hour, up to a maximum of $15 per day. ⌈t⌉ is the least integer greater than or equal to t. Which rule gives the cost C(t) for 0 < t ≤ 24 hours?

choices.text: C(t) = 3⌈t⌉ for 0 < t ≤ 5, and C(t) = 15 for 5 < t ≤ 24
C(t) = 3⌈t⌉ for every t with 0 < t ≤ 24
C(t) = 3t for 0 < t ≤ 5, and C(t) = 15 for 5 < t ≤ 24
C(t) = 3⌊t⌋ for 0 < t ≤ 5, and C(t) = 15 for 5 < t ≤ 24

questions.correct_answer: C(t) = 3⌈t⌉ for 0 < t ≤ 5, and C(t) = 15 for 5 < t ≤ 24
questions.grading_note: Each started hour costs $3 until the $15 maximum at 5 hours. The others round down, charge for exact time, or ignore the maximum.
